answer: An agent begins its network voyage by asking for entry. The host gateway responds by sending a random nonce. The agent then signs this data strictly inside its uncopyable secure enclave. Software spoofing is a fable because extracting one physical key costs attackers 500 dollars and 14 days of lab work. Hitting this operational nadir means attackers hit a physical wall.
